item.research_question: How can an equimolar-ratio high-entropy design strategy be utilized to overcome the bottleneck of low breakdown strength and poor energy density in dielectric ceramics, specifically within tetragonal tungsten bronze structures?
item.material_system: (Sr0.2Ba0.2Pb0.2La0.2Na0.2)Nb2O6 (SBPLNN), a high-entropy tungsten bronze-type relaxor ferroelectric with five equimolar A-site elements (Sr2+, Ba2+, Pb2+, La3+, Na+)
item.processing_route: Traditional solid-state method: raw compounds (SrCO3, BaCO3, Pb3O4, La2O3, Na2CO3, Nb2O5) were ball-milled for 4 h, calcined at 1160 °C for 3 h, ball-milled again for 6 h, pressed with 6.5 wt% PVA binder into 13 mm diameter pellets, and sintered at 1220 °C for 3 h
item.test_conditions: Dielectric properties measured from −120 °C to 200 °C and 10 Hz to 1 MHz; P-E loops and breakdown strength tested up to ~753 kV·cm−1; fatigue tested up to 10^6 cycles at 470 kV·cm−1; temperature stability from −120 °C to 120 °C; frequency stability from 10 Hz to 250 Hz; charge-discharge tested with 300 Ω load resistance
key_findings: Achieved a giant recoverable energy density (Wrec) of 11.0 J·cm−3 and a high efficiency (η) of 81.9% under an electric field of ~753 kV·cm−1.
Configurational entropy (ΔSmix) reached 1.61R due to the introduction of five equimolar elements, driving entropy-dominated phase stabilization.
Grain size was refined to an average of ~1.57 μm with an equiaxed feature, contrasting with the anisometric rod grains of typical TTB ceramics.
Dielectric loss was suppressed to ~0.0014 at room temperature and 1 kHz, with a diffuse dielectric peak showing a large ΔT value of 60.5 °C.
Leakage current density was suppressed to ~2.9 × 10-8 A·cm−2 at 50 kV·cm−1, which is 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than other reported compositions.
Demonstrated robust fatigue resistance up to 10^6 cycles with Wrec fluctuating only from 5.51 J·cm−3 to 5.55 J·cm−3.
Achieved an ultra-fast discharge speed with a time to release 90% of energy (t0.9) of 55.8 ns and a power density of 622.21 MW·cm−3.
Atomic-scale analysis confirmed disordered distribution of all five elements in both A1 and A2 sublattices, breaking inherent site selectivity.
item.mechanism: The high configuration entropy induces increased atomic-scale compositional heterogeneity and strong non-periodic lattice distortion. The compositional heterogeneity disrupts long-range ferroelectric order, generating ultrasmall polar nanoregions (PNRs) that reduce polarization hysteresis and remnant polarization. Simultaneously, the lattice distortion causes grain refinement, increases resistivity, suppresses leakage current, and enhances electrical homogeneity, which collectively lead to an ultrahigh breakdown strength.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study or the material system.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the equimolar-ratio element high-entropy strategy is a universal, practical, and efficient method for developing next-generation dielectric materials and highlight the immense potential of tetragonal tungsten bronze-type materials for advanced energy storage applications.
quotes: realizes a giant recoverable energy density of 11.0 J·cm−3 and a high efficiency of 81.9%.
increased atomic-scale compositional heterogeneity from high configuration entropy, which modulates the relaxor features as well as induces lattice distortion
high-entropy effects break the inherent site selectivity of TTB structures and confirm the enhanced local compositional inhomogeneity
